post.caption: Fabergé's name once sold cologne. In 1937, Samuel Rubin founded a perfume company called Fabergé, and the real Fabergé family in Paris learned of it only after the war. Its cologne, Brut, became the best selling cologne in the world. Film star Cary Grant became its creative consultant in 1967, later joined the board, and got the company plane. Brut's profits paid for a film company, and Glenda Jackson won an Oscar for its film A Touch of Class. Farrah Fawcett later signed on for a Fabergé shampoo line. In 1989 the name ended up on household cleaning products, and in 2009 Fabergé launched a high jewelry collection again.
